# A path parameter that happens to end in "Signals" is a path value, not a
# datastar patch-signals callback: it needs no --output-datastar flag, and the
# generated handler parses it from the path like any other parameter.

muxt generate --use-receiver-type=Server
muxt check

exec go test -count=1

-- template.gohtml --
{{define "GET /watch/{chSignals} sse(Watch(ctx, chSignals, execute))"}}{{.Result}}{{end}}
-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- server.go --
package server

import (
	"context"
	"embed"
	"html/template"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templatesFS embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templatesFS, "*"))

type Server struct{}

func (Server) Watch(_ context.Context, chSignals string, execute func(string) error) {
	_ = execute(chSignals)
}
-- template_test.go --
package server

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestSignalsSuffixedPathParam(t *testing.T) {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	TemplateRoutes(mux, Server{})

	req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/watch/updates", nil)
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, req)

	if rec.Code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("GET /watch/updates = %d, want %d", rec.Code, http.StatusOK)
	}
	if body := rec.Body.String(); !strings.Contains(body, "updates") {
		t.Errorf("body %q does not contain the path value %q", body, "updates")
	}
}
